migration.description: Add additive SQLite storage for service-owned model price sync selections, provider filters, quote-provider choices, and discovery/view history.
migration.release_unit_description: System-shared models.dev sync memory and reviewed price synchronization.

durable_state.description: Explicit provider selections, exact model/provider checkbox choices, quote-provider choices, complete-catalog baseline state, and discovered model first-seen/viewed timestamps.
durable_state.storage_implementation: Five additive SQLite tables: models_dev_sync_metadata, models_dev_sync_provider_selections, models_dev_sync_model_selections, models_dev_sync_quote_provider_choices, and models_dev_sync_discovered_models.

source_compatibility_range.from_program_versions: Earlier repository versions with the managed model and pricing tables but without sync-memory tables.
source_compatibility_range.to_program_version: Candidate release implementing service-owned model sync memory.

ddl_structural_changes.description: Create the singleton metadata table, provider-selection table, composite-key model-selection table, per-model quote-provider table, and per-model discovery/view table with CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS in one SQLite transaction.

dml_changes.description: After the first successful complete normalized catalog retrieval, atomically establish the model-ID baseline as viewed and initialize currently present providers as selected. Do not infer model checkbox choices from local prices or proxy presets.

For later successful complete catalogs, insert newly encountered exact model IDs as unviewed without removing absent records. Apply sparse selection and provider-choice upserts by their documented keys; viewed acknowledgments only advance existing discovery rows and preserve unrelated records.

historical_data_backfill_or_transformati.description: No legacy selection is inferred or backfilled. Existing managed models, preset membership, prices, and historical invocation costs are not changed by sync-memory initialization or updates.

progress_signals: Schema inspection confirms all five additive tables and the singleton metadata row exist.
The metadata flags distinguish an uninitialized baseline/provider set from an intentionally empty provider selection.
A successful initial preview marks its complete candidate model-ID set as the baseline; a later new ID remains unviewed until an actual viewport acknowledgment.
A failed retrieval or parse does not call catalog initialization and leaves discovery history unchanged.
Sparse patch and restart tests confirm explicit false selections and unrelated records survive.
pause_points: After idempotent table creation and before the first successful explicit catalog preview.
Each successful complete catalog observation and each user patch is one bounded SQLite transaction.

recovery.program_rollback_state_behavior: Earlier binaries ignore the additive sync-memory tables and retain their existing managed model, pricing, preset, and history behavior. They do not interpret or rewrite the new sync-memory records.
recovery.faulty_release_recovery: A forward release may re-enter idempotent table creation. Catalog baseline and subsequent discovery updates are transactional; do not drop the new tables or infer checkbox choices during recovery. Existing applied prices and historical costs remain unchanged.

required_test_evidence: The stateful-sqlite profile confirms idempotent schema initialization and restart persistence for selected and explicitly deselected choices.
The first successful catalog baseline, later exact-ID discovery, provider initialization, and viewed acknowledgment are covered without modifying prices or presets.
Concurrent independent patches preserve both keys, and same-key successful writes resolve in commit order.
The sync-state API shares one service-instance state across clients and rejects cross-origin browser writes.
The relevant API, web, and compatibility checks pass for the candidate source range.
